standard.title: Performance skills for characters
standard.description: develop performance skills and/or techniques to manipulate elements of drama and/or use conventions to communicate the physical and psychological aspects of roles and characters consistent with intentions
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can develop performance skills relevant to selected drama styles and forms (Y7-8). They can develop vocal quality, movement skills, and use improvisation to explore character.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students develop performance skills and techniques to communicate the physical and psychological aspects of roles and characters consistent with their dramatic intentions.

nodes.label: Physical and psychological character preparation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can analyse character to identify both physical and psychological dimensions, and use that analysis to ground performance choices.
nodes.minimum_width: Student uses text analysis or improvisation to identify at least two physical and two psychological dimensions of a character, and applies these in a short scene.
nodes.typical_width: Students use analysis of examined text and performances to provide information for exploring the implied and underlying aspects of character; they refine understanding of human behaviours and emotions using appropriate boundaries; they use character analysis to ground voice, physicality and relationship choices.
wider: Students explore how contemporary performance styles and non-realistic conventions can reshape meaning for a character from a classic text
Students investigate how comedy forms (physical comedy, satire, irony) require specific physical and psychological approaches distinct from dramatic character work
nodes.hinge_reason: The move from externally-imposed role-playing to internally-grounded character work is the key development at Y9-10; without psychological grounding, physical performance choices are decorative rather than expressive — the character lacks coherence across the full range of dramatic action.

response_modes.reason: Use character analysis frameworks (Stanislavski objectives, given circumstances, subtext) or equivalent structured approaches before performance work; make the interior life explicit before asking students to express it physically.

success_criteria: Student identifies at least two physical and two psychological dimensions of a character through analysis
Student demonstrates at least one performance choice grounded in psychological analysis (not just physical imitation)

nodes.label: Refining skills for style-specific and convention-based performance
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can refine and adapt their performance skills for specific styles and conventions, achieving coherence between character intention and physical/vocal execution.
nodes.minimum_width: Student applies and refines at least two style-specific techniques across multiple rehearsal iterations, demonstrating measurable improvement in consistency.
nodes.typical_width: Students experiment with, reflect on and refine styles and conventions explored in class; they workshop comedy forms, physical theatre, non-realistic conventions or others; they refine voice through warm-ups focusing on character and delivery; they shape action using analysed conventions.
wider: Students perform the same character through two different stylistic conventions (realism and physical theatre, or naturalism and Brechtian), reflecting on how style shapes character expression

Students develop a character who must communicate both individual psychology and cultural or collective identity simultaneously — as in many First Nations, Asian or community-based dramatic traditions

response_modes.reason: Style-specific refinement requires iterative practice with focused feedback; each rehearsal session should target a specific technical dimension rather than running the full work.
Developing performance skills across multiple styles and conventions — including non-Western or contemporary forms — builds substantially richer expressive range.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The range of performance styles, conventions and cultural dramatic traditions available at Y9-10 is very broad; students who develop skills across multiple styles have substantially richer expressive resources for independent drama-making.
success_criteria: Student applies at least two style-specific techniques with consistency across a rehearsed piece
Student can articulate the connection between their technique choices and the character's physical and psychological dimensions
